answer: Rotating Beacon Admission. Each cycle a public beacon emits fresh verifiable randomness after identities register; the kernel maps that output to a lottery that admits a limited cohort for the next epoch. Because the draw is unpredictable until the beacon fires, an attacker cannot precompute which identities land in the jetty of admitted slots, so mass pre-registration buys no edge. Every attempt costs a full registration transaction plus a deposit that sits idle through the lagoon of each lost draw, making sustained sybil volume linear in real spend.
